notes.meaning: Paul gives Timothy a very serious command in the presence of God and Jesus Christ. Jesus is the one who will judge every person, both those who are alive and those who have died. Timothy is told to carry out his ministry with Christ's return and His royal rule in mind.

differ.view: Some Baptists see Christ's kingdom here as His future thousand-year reign on earth, beginning with the judgment of believers and ending with the judgment of the wicked.
Anglicans traditionally understand this as the eternal, everlasting kingdom of Christ that has no end.

notes.meaning: Paul tells Timothy to preach God's message with urgency. He must proclaim it like a royal herald, whether the timing feels easy or difficult. He must also correct errors, warn wrongdoers, and encourage believers with deep patience and faithful teaching.

A time is coming when people will refuse to put up with healthy, sound teaching from God. Instead, they will follow their own desires and look for speakers who tell them only what they want to hear. They will pile up popular teachers just to satisfy their curious, itching ears.

Because people dislike the truth, they will shut their ears to it. They will wander away to foolish myths and made-up stories instead. Turning away from God's truth leaves people open to believing harmful nonsense.

Timothy must keep a cool head and stay spiritually alert in every situation. He must be willing to suffer hardship and do the work of an evangelist, which means sharing the good news of salvation in Jesus. Paul urges him to carry out every duty of his ministry without quitting.

Paul knows that his life on earth is almost over. He compares his coming death to a drink offering, where wine was poured out as a gift to God. He views dying not as a defeat, but as untying a ship's ropes to head home to heaven.

Paul looks back over his life like a runner finishing an athletic contest. He fought the good fight against sin, completed the race God assigned him, and guarded the true gospel message. He stayed loyal to his Master all the way to the end.

Paul knows a victor's crown of righteousness is waiting for him in heaven. The Lord is the true and fair Judge who will give him this reward when He returns. This prize is not only for Paul, but for all believers who eagerly look forward to Christ's coming.

differ.view: Reformed Christians teach that this crown is given solely by God's free grace through Christ's righteousness, not because human works have earned it.
Methodists teach that God promises this crown as a reward to those who faithfully use and keep the grace He has given them.

notes.meaning: Paul urges Timothy to do everything he can to visit him soon. The apostle was lonely in his cold Roman prison and deeply missed his trusted companion. He also wanted to give Timothy important final directions for the churches face to face.

Paul explains why he is so alone: a helper named Demas abandoned him because he loved the comfort and safety of this present world. Other coworkers had left for ministry tasks, with Crescens going to Galatia and Titus heading to Dalmatia. These departures left Paul with very few helpers in Rome.

Only Luke, the beloved doctor and writer, remained with Paul in Rome. Paul asks Timothy to find Mark and bring him along on the trip. Even though Paul and Mark had parted ways years before, Mark had proven himself faithful and was now very helpful in ministry.

Paul notes that he sent his coworker Tychicus to the city of Ephesus. Tychicus could take over leadership duties there while Timothy traveled to Rome. Paul made sure the local believers were cared for even while he sat in chains.

Paul asks Timothy to pick up the heavy coat he had left with a man named Carpus in Troas. He also asks for his books and especially his animal-skin parchments, which likely contained the Scriptures. Even near the end of his life, Paul cared about keeping warm and studying God's word.

Paul warns Timothy about a metalworker named Alexander who had caused him great harm. Instead of seeking personal revenge, Paul leaves this man to God's justice. He trusts that the Lord will repay everyone fairly according to what they have done.

Paul tells Timothy to watch out for Alexander as well. This man was dangerous because he fiercely opposed the message of the gospel preached by the apostles. Christians must stay alert against people who try to tear down the truth of Christ.

During Paul's first hearing in the Roman court, not a single earthly friend stood by his side to defend him. Everyone ran away out of fear for their own lives. Instead of holding a grudge, Paul lovingly prayed that God would forgive them for deserting him.

Even though human friends failed him, the Lord stood right beside Paul and gave him inner strength. This allowed Paul to proclaim the gospel boldly so that all the Gentile rulers and onlookers could hear it. God protected him at that moment, rescuing him from immediate execution.

Paul trusts that the Lord will keep him safe from every evil trap and bring him safely into His heavenly kingdom. He knows he might be put to death physically, but God will keep his soul and faith secure. Paul bursts into praise, giving glory to Christ forever.

Paul sends warm greetings to his longtime ministry partners, Prisca and Aquila. He also greets the family of Onesiphorus, who had shown him great kindness and courage during his imprisonment. Even facing death, Paul showed deep care for his faithful friends.

Paul shares news about two other close companions. Erastus stayed behind in Corinth, while Paul had to leave Trophimus behind in Miletus because he was sick. Even the apostles could not always cure every illness, showing that healing depends on God's will.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some popular modern teachers claim that God always wills physical healing for believers with enough faith, but traditional commentators point out that Paul had to leave a godly coworker sick.

notes.meaning: Paul repeats his plea for Timothy to arrive before winter begins, since winter storms would stop all ship travel and leave Paul without his warm cloak. He also sends greetings from Roman Christians, including Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and the rest of the church family.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic tradition identifies the Linus mentioned here as the person who succeeded Peter as the bishop of Rome.

notes.meaning: Paul ends his letter by asking the Lord Jesus to be close to Timothy's spirit. He then prays for God's grace, which is His free favor and help, to be with all the believers in the church. Every Christian needs the continuous presence and power of Christ to finish their race.
